title: Grade 5 ELA — Why Authors Write and How You Can Tell
subject: English Language Arts
description: Practice with questions on purpose, audience, persuade, explain, entertain.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: “We should plant a tree near the benches. Its shade would keep them cooler at lunch.” Why did the author most likely write this?
choices: to tell a story about a tree
to explain how to measure a bench
to persuade people to plant a tree
to describe a tree that already grew there

questions.question: “We should plant a tree near the benches. Its shade would keep them cooler at lunch.” Which words best signal that purpose?
choices: “at lunch”
“keep them cooler”
“We should plant”
“near the benches”

questions.question: “When warm air cools, some water vapor becomes tiny drops. A group of these drops can form a cloud.” What is the main purpose?
choices: to explain how clouds can form
to tell a story about one storm
to convince people to stay inside
to teach readers how to make a kite

questions.question: “When warm air cools, some water vapor becomes tiny drops. A group of these drops can form a cloud.” Who would most likely use this text?
choices: a student learning about weather
a driver looking for a street address
a coach planning a game schedule
a cook choosing a soup recipe

questions.question: “The goose stole the mayor's hat and wore it to the parade. By noon, the mayor was marching in a nest.” What is the main purpose?
choices: to report election results
to explain goose behavior using data
to teach readers to weave hats
to entertain with an unlikely story

questions.question: “The goose stole the mayor's hat and wore it to the parade. By noon, the mayor was marching in a nest.” Which feature supports the purpose?
choices: a humorous and unlikely event
a set of repair steps
a chart with facts
a warning in bold text

questions.question: “Step 1: Fill the tray halfway. Step 2: Place seeds on the soil. Step 3: Add a thin layer of soil.” What is the author trying to do?
choices: persuade readers to buy a tray
tell a folktale
compare three kinds of seeds
guide readers through planting seeds

questions.question: “Step 1: Fill the tray halfway. Step 2: Place seeds on the soil. Step 3: Add a thin layer of soil.” Which feature serves this purpose most directly?
choices: a price sticker
a drawing of shade
an author biography
numbered steps

questions.question: “Return books by Friday so others can check them out. Leave returns in the basket by the door.” Where would this message be most useful?
choices: on a notice for library borrowers
on a road map
in a book catalog's subject index
in a story about gardening

questions.question: “Return books by Friday so others can check them out. Leave returns in the basket by the door.” What is the purpose of including “by Friday”?
choices: give readers a deadline
name a type of book
tell readers who wrote it
show how the basket was made

questions.question: “Return books by Friday so others can check them out. Leave returns in the basket by the door.” Which line is mainly meant to persuade?
choices: The station stands beside the sink.
Our class counted twelve cups on Thursday.
Choose the refill station so our class uses fewer cups.
Water flows when the button is pressed.

questions.question: “Return books by Friday so others can check them out. Leave returns in the basket by the door.” Which text would best inform a reader about where oak trees grow?
choices: a fictional scene about a talking oak
a guide with maps and habitat descriptions
a poem comparing oak leaves to hands
an ad selling oak furniture

questions.question: “Return books by Friday so others can check them out. Leave returns in the basket by the door.” What is the likely purpose of a photo caption naming each part of a bicycle?
choices: to argue every person needs a bicycle
to identify parts readers can see
to entertain with a riddle
to recount a race finish

questions.question: “Return books by Friday so others can check them out. Leave returns in the basket by the door.” Which is most useful to readers deciding whether to join an after-school club?
choices: the price of a bus ticket in another city
the age of a different club's founder
meeting times and examples of activities
the hall's paint color

questions.question: “Return books by Friday so others can check them out. Leave returns in the basket by the door.” Which line mainly explains a cause?
choices: I slipped twice and laughed.
The path became muddy because of heavy rain.
Let's close the path today.
Bring boots when you walk the path.

questions.question: An article describes two bus routes, with the costs and times for each. What is its likely purpose?
choices: to make readers laugh
to help readers compare travel options
to persuade everyone to choose the same bus
to describe bus engine parts

questions.question: “Only three days left to support our shelter! Your gift can pay for food and blankets.” What does the author want readers to do?
choices: learn how days are counted
compare fabric types
draw a picture of a blanket
donate to the shelter

questions.question: “I remember the squeak of the porch swing on summer nights, and the cool wood under my bare feet.” What is a likely purpose of these details?
choices: to persuade readers to remove a porch
to compare two towns using data
to teach steps for building a swing
to help readers experience a personal memory

questions.question: “I remember the squeak of the porch swing on summer nights, and the cool wood under my bare feet.” Which headline most clearly signals an explanation?
choices: Vote for a New Park
Come Buy Our Leaf Prints
Why Some Leaves Change Color
The Leaf That Learned to Speak

questions.question: “The trail entrance has moved. Begin your hike beside the visitor center until repairs are finished.” Why does the notice address hikers?
choices: to sell equipment at the center
to direct them to a temporary entrance
to teach where visitors used to live
to entertain them before the hike
